The absence of validated confirmations is attributable primarily to gaps in field team coverage and reporting latency in affected areas, rather than an absence of actual structural damage. Ground conditions, access restrictions, and the compressed operational tempo of the immediate post-landfall period are assessed as contributing factors to incomplete field documentation.

**Key Intelligence Finding: Unreported Structural Damage**

Of significant operational concern, AI-assisted analysis has identified **one (1) structure** exhibiting indicators of severe-to-moderate damage that was **not captured in any submitted field report**, constituting an unreported damage finding requiring urgent ground-truth follow-up. Importantly, this location falls within a community still engaged in long-term recovery from Hurricane Ian (2022), where a mix of newly constructed elevated structures and legacy damaged properties may complicate field team damage classification. This discrepancy between AI-detected indicators and field reporting represents a material gap in the current damage inventory and warrants immediate resolution prior to any PA/IA threshold determinations.

**Confidence Methodology and Recommended Follow-Up Actions**

Damage confidence scores were derived through a weighted multi-source corroboration methodology, wherein convergence across video analysis, satellite change detection, and field reporting yields higher confidence ratings, while source disagreement or absence of field data triggers a downward confidence adjustment and flags the record for manual review. A confidence threshold of 0.70 or greater is applied to elevate findings to priority follow-up status.
